item.title: Fijiana suffer second Test defeat after 29–22 loss to Springbok Women in Lautoka
item.description: The Vodafone Fijiana XV fought hard until the final whistle but were unable to hold off a strong second-half performance from the Springbok Women, going down 29–22 in a closely contested Test in Lautoka this afternoon. Fijiana made an impressive start, with winger Atelaite Buna crossing for the opening try in the third minute to give Fiji an early 5–0 lead .
item.content:encoded:
The Vodafone Fijiana XV fought hard until the final whistle but were unable to hold off a strong second-half performance from the Springbok Women, going down 29–22 in a closely contested Test in Lautoka this afternoon.

Fijiana made an impressive start, with winger Atelaite Buna crossing for the opening try in the third minute to give Fiji an early 5–0 lead .

South Africa struggled to capitalise on its early territorial advantage, making several basic errors during the opening stages.

The Springbok Women eventually found their way over the line in the 18th minute through their hooker to level the match at 5–5.

Fijiana continued to enjoy possession and pressure, but struggled to convert their opportunities into points.

Their persistence paid off in the 28th minute when Vani Buleki scored in the corner, restoring Fiji’s lead at 10–5.

Fijiana held on to that advantage into half-time.

However, South Africa returned from the break with renewed intensity.

Their winger used her pace out wide to score in the 44th minute, putting the Springbok Women ahead for the first time at 12–10.

South Africa then extended its advantage with another try through their winger before Fijiana responded to level the scores at 17–17.

With the match entering its final stages, both sides battled for possession as the contest remained finely balanced.

The Springbok Women regained the lead with another try to move 24–17 ahead.

Fijiana refused to surrender and hit back with nine minutes remaining, cutting the deficit to just two points at 24–22.

But South Africa held its composure under pressure and sealed the victory with a late try to secure a 29–22 win.

Despite the defeat, Fijiana showed determination and resilience throughout the contest, pushing the Springbok Women until the closing stages.

This is the second Test match the Fijiana team has lost against South Africa in Fiji.

item.title: RKS to meet Grammar in U17 Super Deans final
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 15/08/2026 Ratu Kadavulevu School are through to the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans U17 final after defeating Ba Methodist High School 47-29.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 15/08/2026

Ratu Kadavulevu School are through to the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans U17 final after defeating Ba Methodist High School 47-29.

The boys from Delanakaikai started strongly, scoring three tries in the first half to lead 21-12 at half-time.

Ba managed to regroup in the second half and played some spectacular rugby, but the boys from RKS maintained their momentum until the final whistle.

Meanwhile, Suva Grammar School overcame Queen Victoria School 32-24 in the second semi-final to book their place in next week’s final .

In other results, QVS defeated MGM High School 22-15, while Ratu Navula edged RKS 26-25 in the U14 semi-finals.

RKS came from behind to edge rivals Queen Victoria School 28-26, while Marist Brothers High School defeated Lelean Memorial School 16-3 in the U15 semi-finals.

QVS beat MGM High School 17-15, while Suva Grammar thrashed Nasinu Secondary School 22-0 in the U16 semi-finals.

The U18 semi-finals will see Suva Grammar School take on Ra High School at 3pm at Churchill Park, while Lelean Memorial School will meet Nasinu Secondary School at 3.40pm at HFC Bank Stadium.

item.title: Rewa ready for do-or-die clash against Lae City
item.description: Rewa FC captain Setareki Hughes says the side knows it is a do-or-die match when they face Papua New Guinea’s Lae City FC for a place in the OFC Men’s Champions League semi-finals this afternoon . Hughes says they know the task ahead will not be easy as Lae City are a good team, but Rewa will stick to their game plan and work hard to get the result they need.
item.content:encoded:
Rewa FC captain Setareki Hughes says the side knows it is a do-or-die match when they face Papua New Guinea’s Lae City FC for a place in the OFC Men’s Champions League semi-finals this afternoon .

Hughes says they know the task ahead will not be easy as Lae City are a good team, but Rewa will stick to their game plan and work hard to get the result they need.

He says the key will be staying composed throughout the match as they know the win will not come easily.

Hughes says the players are determined to make their supporters proud and will give everything to secure a place in the semi-finals.

Rewa FC will face Lae City FC at 3pm this afternoon at 4R Stadium, Govind Park in Ba.

Navitalai Naivalurua · 15/08/2026

Queen Victoria School had to dig deep to secure their place in the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union U16 final, defeating MGM High School 17-15 at Buckhurst Ground.

The match gave fans what they came for, as both teams showcased some superb rugby.

The match came down to the wire, but costly mistakes denied MGM the win.

QVS slotted a penalty with just a few seconds remaining to secure the victory over MGM.

Meanwhile, Suva Grammar School booked their place in the U16 final after dominating Nasinu Secondary School 22-0.

In other results, QVS defeated MGM High School 22-15, while Ratu Navula College edged RKS 26-25 in the U14 semi-finals. RKS came from behind to edge rivals Queen Victoria School 28-26, while Marist Brothers High School defeated Lelean Memorial School 16-3 in the U15 semi-finals.

The U18 semi-finals will see Suva Grammar School take on Ra High School at 3pm at Churchill Park, while Lelean Memorial School will meet Nasinu Secondary School at 3.40pm at HFC Bank Stadium.

item.title: Nasinu no stranger to Super Deans semi-final pressure
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 14/08/2026 Playing in the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans semi-finals is nothing new for Nasinu Secondary School, as they were the runners-up in last year’s Under-18 grade, losing to Ratu Kadavulevu School 53-15 in the final.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 14/08/2026

Playing in the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans semi-finals is nothing new for Nasinu Secondary School, as they were the runners-up in last year’s Under-18 grade, losing to Ratu Kadavulevu School 53-15 in the final.

Nasinu will field three teams in tomorrow's semi-finals with the school’s Under-18 side set to take on Eastern Zone champions Lelean Memorial School.

They will also feature in the Deans Under-16 grade, where they will meet Suva Grammar School at 10.45am at the HFC Bank Stadium, while their Raluve Under-16 side will face Adi Cakobau School at 9am at Buckhurst Park.

Meanwhile, the Lelean Under-18 side is the only undefeated team heading into the national semi-finals.

Lelean will face Nasinu at 3.40pm tomorrow at the HFC Bank Stadium, while Ra High School will take on Grammar at 3pm at Churchill Park.
